As we have become familiar
with the design of a two-
stage amplifier, we can
easily extend this design
method to three-stage
amplifiers. Indeed, we will
use the Miller effect twice.
The resulting power con-
sumption will be relatively
high as we have to deal with
the two non-dominant
poles. In Chapter 10 on
multistage amplifiers, we
will present some more
multistage amplifiers with
much lower power con-
sumption.
commentary_segments.text: As we have become familiar with the design of a twostage amplifier, we can easily extend this design method to three-stage amplifiers. Indeed, we will use the Miller effect twice. The resulting power consumption will be relatively high as we have to deal with the two non-dominant poles. In Chapter 10 on multistage amplifiers, we will present some more multistage amplifiers with much lower power consumption.
